The task asks for a rank-minimal exact tensor decomposition for multiplying a $2 \times 2$ matrix ($A$) by a $2 \times 11$ matrix ($B$).
Let the dimensions be $n=2$ (rows of $A$), $m=2$ (cols of $A$, rows of $B$), $p=11$ (cols of $B$).
The tensor shape is $(n \times m) \times (m \times p) \times (p \times n) = 4 \times 22 \times 22$.
The schoolbook algorithm has rank $n \times m \times p = 44$.

We can improve this by using Strassen's algorithm for the $2 \times 2$ multiplication part.
Strassen's algorithm computes the product of two $2 \times 2$ matrices using 7 multiplications instead of 4.
For a $2 \times 2$ matrix $A$ and a $2 \times 11$ matrix $B$, we can view the multiplication as 11 independent $2 \times 2$ multiplications (one for each column of $B$).
However, Strassen's algorithm allows us to compute the product of a $2 \times 2$ matrix and a $2 \times k$ matrix with $7k$ multiplications? No, that's not quite right.
Let's look at the structure.
$A = \begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix}$, $B = \begin{pmatrix} B_1 \\ B_2 \end{pmatrix}$ where $B_1, B_2$ are $1 \times 11$ row vectors.
The product $C = A B = \begin{pmatrix} a B_1 + b B_2 \\ c B_1 + d B_2 \end{pmatrix}$.
This requires 4 vector multiplications (scalar times vector) and 2 vector additions.
The tensor decomposition rank corresponds to the number of scalar multiplications.
In the schoolbook approach, we have 4 scalar multiplications per column of $B$, so $4 \times 11 = 44$ multiplications.
